rate (fps)"},{"name":"general_help","value":"" <body> <h1><u>How to use Bimostitch</u></h1> NOTE: When (Pro) is appended to the beginning of a word/statement or just after a dash or dot, then the feature is available only on the Pro version of the app.<br/><br/>
        &#8226; Bimostitch is a fully automated panorama stitcher that enables you to automatically stitch individual overlapping images or (Pro) video into panoramas.<br/><br/>
        &#8226; You can stitch overlapping photos from any source such as drones, cameras, downloaded photos, old photos and photos from other apps.<br/><br/>
        &#8226; Select photos or a (Pro) video by pressing the gallery icon, located on the top-right of the apps home screen, then the app will automatically do the stitching.<br/><br/>
        &#8226; You need to make sure the photos share some common overlapping areas, else the app will ignore them automatically.<br/><br/>
        &#8226; You can turn on/off the preview mode that enables you to quickly preview the panorama before final rendering.<br/><br/>
        &#8226; There are various rendering options to choose from such as seam detection mode which controls how the app locates cutting points for each image. Make sure to select (Pro) Optimal seam detection for best results.<br/><br/>
        &#8226; (Pro) Optimal seam detection allows the app to find the best places to cut in order to minimize visible seams.<br/><br/>
        &#8226; Voronoi just uses a naive line that cuts alone points of equal distance from closest image centers.<br/><br/>
        &#8226; Image borders simply uses the image outline as a seam line.<br/><br/> NOTE: Blending is off for Image border seam detection since its very difficult to blend along image borders.<br/><br/> (Pro) You can control the amount of blending the app applies to the image using the Blending Strength slider. To turn on/off blending there is a toggle switch.<br/><br/>
        &#8226; You can also select between the following projection options, equirectangular (projects images onto a spherical surface), cylindrical (projects images onto a cylindrical surface), planar (projects images onto a plane) and auto-detect ( selects between the above mentioned projection options). <br/><br/>
        &#8226; Balancing options include auto-straighten, auto-crop, auto-exposure, (Pro) auto-color.<br/><br/>

strings.name: general_help
strings.value:
" <body> <h1><u>How to use Bimostitch</u></h1> NOTE: When (Pro) is appended to the beginning of a word/statement or just after a dash or dot, then the feature is available only on the Pro version of the app.<br/><br/>
        &#8226; Bimostitch is a fully automated panorama stitcher that enables you to automatically stitch individual overlapping images or (Pro) video into panoramas.<br/><br/>
        &#8226; You can stitch overlapping photos from any source such as drones, cameras, downloaded photos, old photos and photos from other apps.<br/><br/>
        &#8226; Select photos or a (Pro) video by pressing the gallery icon, located on the top-right of the apps home screen, then the app will automatically do the stitching.<br/><br/>
        &#8226; You need to make sure the photos share some common overlapping areas, else the app will ignore them automatically.<br/><br/>
        &#8226; You can turn on/off the preview mode that enables you to quickly preview the panorama before final rendering.<br/><br/>
        &#8226; There are various rendering options to choose from such as seam detection mode which controls how the app locates cutting points for each image. Make sure to select (Pro) Optimal seam detection for best results.<br/><br/>
        &#8226; (Pro) Optimal seam detection allows the app to find the best places to cut in order to minimize visible seams.<br/><br/>
        &#8226; Voronoi just uses a naive line that cuts alone points of equal distance from closest image centers.<br/><br/>
        &#8226; Image borders simply uses the image outline as a seam line.<br/><br/> NOTE: Blending is off for Image border seam detection since its very difficult to blend along image borders.<br/><br/> (Pro) You can control the amount of blending the app applies to the image using the Blending Strength slider. To turn on/off blending there is a toggle switch.<br/><br/>
        &#8226; You can also select between the following projection options, equirectangular (projects images onto a spherical surface), cylindrical (projects images onto a cylindrical surface), planar (projects images onto a plane) and auto-detect ( selects between the above mentioned projection options). <br/><br/>
        &#8226; Balancing options include auto-straighten, auto-crop, auto-exposure, (Pro) auto-color.<br/><br/>
        &#8226; Auto-straighten tries to find a common plane in which the panorama was taken then renders it relative to that plane ie if you shoot photos sweeping left to right the common plane is aligned with the horizon. <br/><br/>
        &#8226; Auto-crop finds the best possible way to crop the panorama with minimal loss in resolution.<br/><br/>
        &#8226; Auto-exposure normalizes the exposure differences between images. It is recommended to capture images with uniform exposure for best results.<br/><br/>
        &#8226; (Pro) Auto-color tries to normalize the colors across the entire panorama. Again it is best to have images with uniform colors to begin with for best results.<br/><br/>
        &#8226; The settings, auto-straighten, auto-crop, auto-exposure, (Pro) auto-color, can all be turned on/off with a toggle and the (Pro) sliders help control their effect on the images. The preview allows you to quickly check which settings are best.<br/><br/>
        &#8226; The output options allows you to control the maximum output resolution, the album name, (Pro) the output image format and (Pro) compression quality to control the size of the rendered panoramas, in order to save space on your device set it at 80%.<br/><br/>
        &#8226; The preview allows you to quickly check between different settings before final rendering. (Pro) You can check the source images and save the preview for later rendering. You can turn on/off the preview mode in the settings. When off the app will directly render the panorama as specified by the main defaults (user settings).<br/><br/>
        &#8226; (Pro) The app can stitch a video of panning motion into a panorama. You can shoot a video, panning around about a fixed point and this app will turn it into a wide angle panorama output automatically.<br/><br/> For faster video stitching you can change the sampling rate for the video to lower fps, higher fps will slow down stitching since the app now needs to sample more frames per second ie it takes time to process each incoming frame.<br/><br/> You can also change the overlap ratio threshold between frames. This enables the app to identify key frames which are frames that are sufficiently seperated ie overlap ratio between them is just below threshold. Non-key frames are frames whose overlap ratio to the closest key frame is above the threshold. A higher overlap ratio threshold means more key frames being detected hence slower.<br/><br/>
        &#8226; (Pro) You can also control the quality of the optimal seam detection mentioned above in the advanced options.<br/><br/> This only controls the resolution at which the seam is computed. Lower quality is good enough and also provides speed improvements. The higher quality options are slower but may provide a better output panorama overall.<br/><br/>
        &#8226; Panoramas are stored in the app specific folders (albums), to share them outside the app, while in app, press the standard share button on the bottom right side of the frame containing the panorama thumbnail in order to trigger the export dialog. You can then either save to a folder outside the app where other apps have access or send directly to any app listed in the export dialog.<br/><br/> To delete a panorama, press and hold to trigger a delete dialog then press confirm or cancel.<br/><br/>
        &#8226; The app only embeds associated panorama XMP metadata, for 3D VR viewers, only if the following conditions are satisfied, the panorama is in equirectangular (spherical) projection, the panorama is horizontally aligned and the stitching algorithm recovers a valid field of view.<br/><br/>
        &#8226; (Pro) Auto lens calibration helps to compensate and correct for lens distortions introduced by wide-angle, ultra wide-angle and fisheye lens.<br/><br/>
        &#8226; The app's viewer does not displace panoramas in full resolution, to view panoramas in full resolution use external viewers.<br/><br/> </body> "

strings.name: tips_help
strings.value:
" <body> <h1><u>Tips for stitching better panoramas</u></h1> The following guidelines will help you make the best possible panoramas with Bimostitch. <br/><br/> &#8226; Photos that are plain or clear in the area of overlap will fail to stitch.<br/><br/>
       &#8226; Non overlapping photos will be automatically ignored. Ensure you capture images with not less than 25% overlap for better results.<br/><br/>
       &#8226; Avoid capturing plain clear photos.<br/><br/>
       &#8226; Avoid too many repeated or very similar looking structures in overlapping photos, this can lead to false matches.<br/><br/>
       &#8226; Use your favorite camera app to capture overlapping images.<br/><br/>
       &#8226; Make sure there is enough overlap area between photos.<br/><br/>
       &#8226; Make sure to hold your phone firmly in landscape or portrait mode and rotate it such that the rotation axis passes through the camera lens. Rotate the camera in any direction but keep the camera lens on the same point as much as possible. Do not use your body as a rotation axis.<br/><br/>
       &#8226; Use the camera lens as the reference point and not your body when capturing photos for stitching. Keep the lens or device at the same point as much as possible but rotate it in any direction to capture overlapping photos.<br/><br/>
       &#8226; Keep the lens or camera still when snapping to avoid motion blur.<br/><br/>
       &#8226; To help capture good overlapping shots keep track of the center of the previous shot and snap another when it reaches the edge.<br/><br/>
       &#8226; Avoid capturing photos in direct sunlight.<br/><br/>
       &#8226; Don’t merge photos with severe differences in lighting conditions.<br/><br/>
       &#8226; Avoid moving objects in the area of overlap.<br/><br/> </body> "
